# bugs #3703: sdas8051: ACALL to a numeric address writes past the relocation buffer and corrupts the location counter or the object file

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3703/
- Category: [Analyzed, not fixed](../../unresolved.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Change outchk(3, 0) to outchk(3, 4) in outrwm in sdas/asxxsrc/asout.c. The change is not tested.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

`sdas8051` built from r17176 assembles the test case of the ticket and reports no error. In the
listing the second `.ORG`, the label `L1`, and the `LJMP` are at 008000. The reporter's listing
from SDCC 4.3.0 has FF808000 in these three lines.

The object file from r17176 is wrong. The T line for the three branches begins with `FF FF 00`
where the address `00 00 00` belongs, and its R line has 18 bytes.

    T FF FF 00 60 00 00 00 20 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
    R 00 00 00 02 F1 07 04 00 00 F1 07 09 00 00 08 0C FF FF

For this file `sdld` warns of a byte PCR relocation error at offsets FFFF00 and FFFF05 and of a 2K
page relocation error at offset FFFF07, and then it ends with a segmentation fault.

Three shorter files were assembled as well. One has only the `JZ` line between the two `.ORG`
lines, one has only the `ACALL` line, and one has a `NOP`. In each listing the second `.ORG` is at
008000, and each T line begins with the correct address. The file with the `JZ` line was linked,
and the branch is resolved to `60 FE`, which is correct.

The tests ran on a Linux host. The reporter's host is not named in the ticket. SDCC 4.3.0 was not
built for a comparison.

## Known

`outrwm` in `sdas/asxxsrc/asout.c` writes past the end of the relocation buffer `rel[]`, which has
16 bytes (`NREL`). In its branch for the 8051 and ds390 targets and an absolute destination, the
function calls `outchk(3, 0)`. The call asks for three free bytes in `txt[]` and for none in
`rel[]`. The function then writes four bytes to `rel[]` with `write_rmode` and `out_rw(0xFFFF)`.
In the test case 14 bytes of `rel[]` are in use after the `JZ` and `JB` lines, and `ACALL 0x0000`
writes bytes 15 to 18. `AJMP` uses the same code and was not run.

The variable that the two bytes after the buffer overwrite depends on the layout of the `sdas8051`
binary. In the binary built for this entry `txt[]` follows `rel[]`, so the bytes replace the
address at the start of the T line. The reporter's result fits a binary in which `s_mask` follows
`rel[]`. `rngchk` in `sdas/asxxsrc/asexpr.c` returns FF808000 for 0x8000 when the low two bytes of
`s_mask` are FF FF. The object file is written only in the last pass, so the value of the second
`.ORG` changes in that pass, which gives the phase error at `L1`. The reporter's binary was not
examined.

r14093, which set the version to 4.3.0, has the same `outchk` call and the same buffer size.

## Open

The call has to ask for the four relocation bytes, for example as `outchk(3, 4)`. The branch for
relocatable destinations in the same function asks for five. No fix was built or tested. The
segmentation fault of `sdld` for the object file above was not examined.

## Related

The two files with `ACALL` show a second problem on r17176, which has no ticket. The opcode byte of
`ACALL` and `AJMP` is 00 in the object file. A file with `acall sub`, `ajmp start`, and `ret` in a
relocatable area links to `00 04 00 00 22`, and `11 04 01 00 22` is correct. r16924 changed the
call in `sdas/as8051/i51mch.c` to `outrwm(&e, R_J11, op << 8)`, and `outrwm` stores that argument
in one byte for the 8051 and ds390 targets.
